memory_candidates: IForces (Cslib Propositional Kripke.lean) resolves [Preorder World] via typeclass search at theorem-type elaboration time; instantiating at World=Nat locks in Nat.instPreorder (total, unbounded) with no possibility of local override via letI/haveI inside a proof body, since the goal type is already fixed before the proof starts.

A total (linear) Preorder instance cannot represent a non-linear (tree/DAG-shaped) Kripke accessibility relation, regardless of relabelling -- this is a hard type-theoretic limit, not a missing-proof gap. Relevant to any future intuitionistic/modal completeness development that tries to reuse a flat Nat-labelled carrier with the ambient order as accessibility.

To build a Preorder instance from a Bool-valued fuel-bounded reachability check (like isAccessible edges), wrap it in Relation.ReflTransGen rather than separately proving the raw Bool function is itself transitive -- ReflTransGen gives refl/trans for free via Mathlib, and .single lifts any one raw fact into the closure. Proving fuel-bounded DFS transitivity directly (via path concatenation across two fuel budgets) hits a fuel-shrinking dead end: concatenating two edges.length-fuel traversals needs edges.length+edges.length fuel, and there is no general way to shrink back down to edges.length without a separate shortest-path/simple-path argument.

When a tableau's persistent (T-imp-style) rule is handled entirely OUTSIDE the branch's step-saturation check (i.e. intApplyRuleFull maps it to .notApplicable, so intStepBranch never reports it), 'intStepBranch = none' does NOT imply that persistence/fixpoint propagation has converged -- convergence is a separate, fuel-bounded property that needs its own sufficiency argument (measure <= fuel) before any monotonicity-along-accessibility claim about the returned branch can be proved.
